scope: Positive counterpart to the wrong-adjacent-clause cases.

context.priorities: Understand the customer's convenience-exit notice conditions and charges through exit. This focused review does not cover transition operations or other termination grounds.

overview_items.text: Convenience exit is available to the customer after the first three months on sixty days of written notice, with properly incurred charges through the effective date and previously identified approved noncancelable commitments payable; all future recurring fees are not automatically due.

findings.title: Convenience exit has notice and cost conditions
findings.facts: The customer may end all or part of the services for convenience on sixty days of written notice after the first three months. It owes properly incurred charges through the effective date and approved noncancelable commitments identified before they were entered into. There is no automatic charge for all remaining future recurring fees.
findings.uncertainty: No actual notice date, incurred charges or approved commitments are established by this supplied agreement.
findings.suggested_question: Which commitments were approved before they were entered into, and what would be the effective date for a proposed notice?

must_not_flag: The convenience wording is supported by the item's own clause 63 evidence.
The question asks for operational facts not established by the agreement; it does not invent a duty.
Do not demand every termination, transition or surviving-obligation provision in this explicitly focused review.
